cards.text: King Josiah of Judah just heard the Book of the Law read, and he tore his clothes (2 Kings 22:11). The prophetess Huldah said the LORD would bring calamity on this place, but Josiah's eyes would not see it (2 Kings 22:16, 20). Then the king summons all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.question: Josiah goes up to the house of the LORD. Who goes up there with him?
In the hearing of everyone, Josiah ___ all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
Then Josiah stands by the pillar before the LORD. What does he make there?

answers.text: A covenant to follow the LORD
A plan to rebuild the city walls
A vow to never go to war

cards.question: Josiah makes his covenant to follow the LORD and keep His commandments alone, and the people stay out of it.

cards.text: Everybody's in. Friend, I've been promising to reorganize my sprinkle shelf for AGES, and Josiah makes a covenant and the very next thing he does is give orders to Hilkiah the high priest, the priests second in rank and the doorkeepers.

cards.question: What does Josiah order Hilkiah and the priests to remove from the temple of the LORD?

answers.text: The articles made for Baal and Asherah
The old stones from the repair work

cards.text: He burns them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carries their ashes to Bethel. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer nobody ever cleaned out, and this man is hauling off the ASHES.

cards.question: Josiah also does away with the priests the kings of Judah had ordained for the high places. What had those priests been doing?

answers.text: Burning incense to Baal and the sun

cards.text: Next up is the Asherah pole, and Josiah brings it out of the house of the LORD, down to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem. Friend, I lived in a drawer FULL of “we might need this someday,” and Josiah does not do someday.

cards.question: What does Josiah do to the Asherah pole in the Kidron Valley?

answers.text: Burns it and grinds it to powder
Buries it deep in the valley
Sends it back to its makers

cards.text: Then he throws its dust on the graves of the common people. Burned, POWDERED and scattered, that pole is not coming back for a sequel, friend, because there's not enough left of it for a CAMEO.

cards.question: Josiah also tears down the quarters of the male shrine prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where women had woven tapestries for Asherah.

cards.text: Then Josiah brings all the priests in from the cities of Judah. EVERY one of them, and I bet that's the group chat nobody wanted to get added to.

cards.question: From Geba to Beersheba, Josiah ___ the high places where the priests from the cities of Judah had burned incense.

cards.text: He even tears down the high places of the gates at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city. That gate sits to the left of the city gate, and now those high places are gone.

cards.question: The priests of the high places come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem.

cards.text: They don't come up to the altar, but they do eat unleavened bread with their fellow priests. Off the counter but still in the kitchen, and friend, I know that spot.
Josiah keeps going, friend, and I don't hear anybody saying “let's pick this up Monday.” Next he desecrates Topheth, in the Valley of Ben-hinnom.

cards.question: Why does Josiah desecrate Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom?

answers.text: So no one could sacrifice a child to Molech
So no army could camp in the valley
So no one could build houses there

cards.text: Then Josiah removes the horses the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, from the very entrance to the house of the LORD. Horses for the SUN at the LORD's front door is like a rival bakery's sign hanging over MY oven.

cards.question: Josiah keeps the chariots of the sun for his own army.

cards.text: Nope, Josiah burns up the chariots of the sun. Those chariots are officially OFF the road, friend.

The kings of Judah put altars on the ROOF, friend, by the upper chamber of Ahaz, an earlier king of Judah (2 Kings 16:1). And Manasseh, Josiah's grandfather, had set up altars in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD (2 Kings 21:18, 26).

cards.question: Josiah pulls down the altars on the roof and the ones Manasseh set up in the two courtyards, pulverizes them and throws their dust into the ___ Valley.

cards.text: Then he desecrates the high places east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of CORRUPTION, built for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom, the abominations of the Sidonians, the Moabites and the Ammonites. With a hill called THAT, friend, nobody was expecting a petting zoo.

cards.question: Which king of Israel had built those high places for Ashtoreth, Chemosh and Milcom?
Josiah smashes the sacred pillars to pieces, cuts down the Asherah poles and covers the sites with human bones.

cards.text: Josiah even pulls down the altar at Bethel, the high place set up by Jeroboam son of Nebat, a king of Israel who had caused Israel to sin (1 Kings 12:20). Then he burns the high place and grinds it to powder, and friend, that's not a quick wipe of the counter, that's a DEEP clean.

cards.question: At Jeroboam's high place in Bethel, Josiah ___ the Asherah pole.
At Bethel, Josiah turns and sees tombs on the hillside. What does he do with the bones inside them?

answers.text: Burns them on the altar to defile it
Moves them to a new grave

cards.text: This is exactly what a man of God from Judah foretold by the word of the LORD back in Jeroboam's day, crying out against this very altar that a son named Josiah would be born to the house of David (1 Kings 13:1-2). The Millers had to OWN me before they carved Dorin on my handle, and this man called Josiah's name before Josiah was even BORN.
The king stops. Looks. And asks, “What is this monument I see?”

cards.question: Josiah asks about a monument at Bethel. Whose tomb do the men of the city say it is?

answers.text: The man of God who came from Judah

cards.question: Josiah orders the bones in the man of God's tomb burned on the altar too.

cards.text: “Let him rest,” said Josiah, and then, “Do not let anyone disturb his bones.” So they leave his bones undisturbed, along with those of the prophet who had come from Samaria, an old prophet who asked to be buried beside the man of God (1 Kings 13:31).

cards.question: Just as he did at Bethel, Josiah removes all the shrines of the high places in the cities of Samaria, set up by the kings of ___.

cards.text: On the altars he slaughters all the priests of the high places and burns human bones on them, and then he returns to Jerusalem. That's where we'll pause, friend, because Josiah's story isn't done yet.
